section_1.title: The Hook: The Speeding Falcon
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of 'instantaneous change' versus 'average change.' Use an animation of a falcon diving to explain why we need more than just basic division to find speed at a single point in time.
section_1.example: A falcon dives along a curved path. We know its average speed between two points, but how fast is it going at exactly 2.5 seconds? This 'instant' is where the derivative begins.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Check: The Slope of a Line
section_2.content: Quickly review the linear slope formula (Rise over Run). This serves as the foundation for understanding how curves behave when zoomed in.
section_2.example: Visualizing a straight ramp with a constant slope of m = Δy/Δx. If you walk 2 meters forward and rise 1 meter, your 'rate of change' is 0.5.

section_3.title: Geometric Intuition: The Magnifying Glass
section_3.content: Transition from a secant line (two points) to a tangent line (one point) using a limit process. Animate a magnifying glass zooming into a curve until the curve looks perfectly straight.
section_3.example: Zooming into the function f(x) = x² at the point (1,1). As we zoom in 1000x, the curve starts to look like a straight line with a slope of 2. This 'local slope' is the derivative.

section_4.title: The Power Rule: Symbolic Shortcut
section_4.content: Introduce the Power Rule formula: d/dx(x^n) = n*x^(n-1). Present this as a 'pattern-matching' tool that replaces complex limit calculations.
section_4.example: If our falcon's position is x³, the derivative (speed) is 3x². If the position is x⁴, the derivative is 4x³.

section_5.title: Visualizing the Formula: The Growing Square
section_5.content: Explain why the derivative of x² is 2x using geometry. Use an expanding square to show that as the side length 'x' increases by a tiny bit 'dx', the area increases by two thin strips.
section_5.example: A square with side x has area x². Increase the sides by a tiny sliver 'dx'. The new area is added on two sides (top and right), each with an area of x * dx. Total change = 2x * dx. Therefore, the rate of change is 2x.

section_6.title: Application and Wrap-up: The Steering Wheel
section_6.content: Summarize how the formula (abstract) and the geometry (visual) represent the same reality. Explain that derivatives allow us to 'steer' and predict changes in technology.
section_6.example: Show a self-driving car adjusting its steering angle based on the 'slope' of the curve ahead. The derivative tells the computer exactly how much to turn at every millisecond.

section_1.title: The Hook: The Speeding Falcon
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of 'instantaneous change' versus 'average change.' Use an animation of a falcon diving to explain why we need more than just basic division to find speed at a single point in time.
section_1.example: A falcon dives along a curved path. We know its average speed between two points, but how fast is it going at exactly 2.5 seconds? This 'instant' is where the derivative begins.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Check: The Slope of a Line
section_2.content: Quickly review the linear slope formula (Rise over Run). This serves as the foundation for understanding how curves behave when zoomed in.
section_2.example: Visualizing a straight ramp with a constant slope of m = Δy/Δx. If you walk 2 meters forward and rise 1 meter, your 'rate of change' is 0.5.

section_3.title: Geometric Intuition: The Magnifying Glass
section_3.content: Transition from a secant line (two points) to a tangent line (one point) using a limit process. Animate a magnifying glass zooming into a curve until the curve looks perfectly straight.
section_3.example: Zooming into the function f(x) = x² at the point (1,1). As we zoom in 1000x, the curve starts to look like a straight line with a slope of 2. This 'local slope' is the derivative.

section_4.title: The Power Rule: Symbolic Shortcut
section_4.content: Introduce the Power Rule formula: d/dx(x^n) = n*x^(n-1). Present this as a 'pattern-matching' tool that replaces complex limit calculations.
section_4.example: If our falcon's position is x³, the derivative (speed) is 3x². If the position is x⁴, the derivative is 4x³.

section_5.title: Visualizing the Formula: The Growing Square
section_5.content: Explain why the derivative of x² is 2x using geometry. Use an expanding square to show that as the side length 'x' increases by a tiny bit 'dx', the area increases by two thin strips.
section_5.example: A square with side x has area x². Increase the sides by a tiny sliver 'dx'. The new area is added on two sides (top and right), each with an area of x * dx. Total change = 2x * dx. Therefore, the rate of change is 2x.

section_6.title: Application and Wrap-up: The Steering Wheel
section_6.content: Summarize how the formula (abstract) and the geometry (visual) represent the same reality. Explain that derivatives allow us to 'steer' and predict changes in technology.
section_6.example: Show a self-driving car adjusting its steering angle based on the 'slope' of the curve ahead. The derivative tells the computer exactly how much to turn at every millisecond.

section_1.title: The Hook: The Speeding Falcon
lecture_lines: Imagine a falcon diving through the air.
We can calculate its average speed easily.
But how fast is it going right now?
animations: Create a dark blue falcon silhouette (#3399FF) at the start of a parabolic path. Highlight the first lecture line.
Show the falcon diving along the path. Draw two points on the curve with gold circles (#FFD700) and a dashed white line. Highlight the second lecture line.
Move the points closer until they merge into a single point, and the line becomes a solid golden tangent line (#FFD700). Highlight the third lecture line.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Check: The Slope of a Line
lecture_lines: The slope measures how steep a line is.
It is the vertical rise over horizontal run.
Constant slope means a constant rate of change.
animations: Draw a white straight line (#FFFFFF) rising at a 30-degree angle. Highlight the first lecture line.
Animate a blue right-angled triangle (#58C4DD) under the line, labeling the vertical side 'dy' and horizontal side 'dx'. Highlight the second lecture line.
Flash the formula 'm = dy / dx' in light green (#87FF65) next to the triangle. Highlight the third lecture line.

section_3.title: Geometric Intuition: The Magnifying Glass
lecture_lines: Finding the slope of a curve is harder.
Let's zoom into this point on the curve.
As we zoom in, the curve looks straighter.
Eventually, it looks like a simple straight line.
This local slope is the derivative at that point.
animations: Draw a red parabola y=x^2 (#FC6255) on a black background. Highlight the first lecture line.
Place two points on the parabola and draw a white secant line through them. Highlight the second lecture line.
A circular magnifying glass border (#E6E6E6) appears around the point (1,1) and scales up to fill the screen, showing the curve flattening. Highlight the third lecture line.
The curve now looks like a straight line. Highlight the fourth lecture line.
Draw a bright yellow tangent line (#FFFF00) over the flattened curve and label its slope as '2'. Highlight the fifth lecture line.

section_4.title: The Power Rule: Symbolic Shortcut
lecture_lines: Calculating limits every time is very slow.
The Power Rule gives us a faster shortcut.
Take the exponent and move it to the front.
Then, subtract one from the original exponent.
For x squared, the derivative is two x.
animations: Display the expression 'x to the power of n' in white (#FFFFFF) in the center of the screen. Highlight the first lecture line.
Show a 'shortcut' arrow (#58C4DD) pointing to the side. Highlight the second lecture line.
Animate the 'n' moving from the exponent to the front of 'x' and changing color to bright orange (#FF8000). Highlight the third lecture line.
Change the remaining exponent to 'n minus 1' in orange (#FF8000). Highlight the fourth lecture line.
Display 'd/dx(x^2) = 2x' as a specific example below the rule. Highlight the fifth lecture line.

section_5.title: Visualizing the Formula: The Growing Square
lecture_lines: Why does the derivative of x squared work?
Consider a square with a side length of x.
If we increase x slightly, the area grows.
The extra area forms two thin rectangles.
These strips represent the two x rate of change.
animations: Draw a blue square (#58C4DD) with sides labeled 'x'. Highlight the first lecture line.
The text 'Area = x^2' appears inside the square in white (#FFFFFF). Highlight the second lecture line.
Expand the top and right edges of the square by a small thickness labeled 'dx' in light blue (#ACE3EE). Highlight the third lecture line.
Highlight the two new rectangular regions on the edges in bright yellow (#FFD700). Highlight the fourth lecture line.
The formula 'd/dx (x^2) = 2x' fades in at the bottom in light green (#87FF65). Highlight the fifth lecture line.

section_6.title: Application and Wrap-up: The Steering Wheel
lecture_lines: Derivatives help us navigate a changing world.
They guide self-driving cars along smooth paths.
Calculus turns complex motion into predictable patterns.
animations: Show a white car icon (#FFFFFF) moving along a winding road line. Highlight the first lecture line.
Draw a bright yellow arrow (#FFD700) pointing in the car's instantaneous direction (tangent). Highlight the second lecture line.
Animate a blue steering wheel (#58C4DD) rotating to match the angle of the yellow arrow. Highlight the third lecture line.

class TeachingScene(Scene):

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Hook: The Speeding Falcon"
        lines = [
            "Imagine a falcon diving through the air.",
            "We can calculate its average speed easily.",
            "But how fast is it going right now?"
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Function for the parabolic path
        # y = 2.2 - 0.2 * (x - 0.5)^2
        # Starts at A1 (0.5, 2.2), ends at F6 (5.5, -2.8)
        def path_func(x):
            return 2.2 - 0.2 * (x - 0.5)**2

        path_curve = FunctionGraph(
            path_func,
            x_range=[0.5, 5.5],
            color=BLUE_E
        )

        # Falcon silhouette representation
        falcon = Triangle(color="#3399FF", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.2)
        falcon.rotate(-PI/2) # Pointing down-right roughly
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Place falcon at start
        self.place_at_grid(falcon, "A1")
        self.add(path_curve, falcon)
        self.play(FadeIn(path_curve), FadeIn(falcon))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Falcon dives along path
        falcon_pos_tracker = ValueTracker(0.5)
        falcon.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(np.array([
            falcon_pos_tracker.get_value(),
            path_func(falcon_pos_tracker.get_value()),
            0
        ])))
        
        # Points for average speed
        p1_x = 1.5
        p2_x = 4.5
        p1 = Dot(np.array([p1_x, path_func(p1_x), 0]), color="#FFD700")
        p2 = Dot(np.array([p2_x, path_func(p2_x), 0]), color="#FFD700")
        
        # Secant line
        secant_line = DashedLine(p1.get_center(), p2.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        
        self.play(
            falcon_pos_tracker.animate.set_value(5.5),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.play(Create(p1), Create(p2))
        self.play(Create(secant_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # ValueTracker for p2's relative position to p1
        dx_tracker = ValueTracker(p2_x - p1_x)
        
        # Updaters for moving elements
        p2.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(np.array([
            p1_x + dx_tracker.get_value(),
            path_func(p1_x + dx_tracker.get_value()),
            0
        ])))
        
        def get_tangent_line():
            start_x = p1_x
            end_x = p1_x + dx_tracker.get_value()
            
            p_start = np.array([start_x, path_func(start_x), 0])
            p_end = np.array([end_x, path_func(end_x), 0])
            
            # If points are identical, use derivative for tangent direction
            if abs(end_x - start_x) < 0.01:
                # derivative dy/dx = -0.4 * (x - 0.5)
                slope = -0.4 * (start_x - 0.5)
                # Tangent line vector (1, slope)
                direction = np.array([1, slope, 0])
                direction = direction / np.linalg.norm(direction)
                line = Line(p_start - direction * 1.5, p_start + direction * 1.5, color="#FFD700")
            else:
                # Secant line extended
                direction = p_end - p_start
                direction = direction / np.linalg.norm(direction)
                line = Line(p_start - direction * 1.0, p_end + direction * 1.0, color=WHITE if dx_tracker.get_value() > 0.1 else "#FFD700")
            
            return line

        # We'll replace secant_line with an always_redraw for smooth transition
        self.remove(secant_line)
        live_line = always_redraw(get_tangent_line)
        self.add(live_line)
        
        # Move falcon back to p1 area for focus
        self.play(
            falcon_pos_tracker.animate.set_value(p1_x),
            dx_tracker.animate.set_value(0.001),
            run_time=4
        )
        
        # Ensure the final state is a solid gold tangent line
        # This is handled by always_redraw and the slope logic.
        
        self.wait(2)

            t = t_tracker.get_value()
            pos = road.point_from_proportion(t / 5)
            # Tangent angle
            epsilon = 0.001
            p1 = road.point_from_proportion(max(0, t / 5 - epsilon))
            p2 = road.point_from_proportion(min(1, t / 5 + epsilon))
            angle = np.arctan2(p2[1] - p1[1], p2[0] - p1[0])
            m.move_to(pos)
            m.set_angle(angle)

        car.add_updater(update_car)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Geometric Intuition: The Magnifying Glass", [
            "Finding the slope of a curve is harder.",
            "Let's zoom into this point on the curve.",
            "As we zoom in, the curve looks straighter.",
            "Eventually, it looks like a simple straight line.",
            "This local slope is the derivative at that point."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Parabola y=x^2
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-0.5, 2.5, 1],
            y_range=[-0.5, 4.5, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY_D},
            x_length=5,
            y_length=5
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6")
        
        parabola = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2, x_range=[-0.5, 2.1], color="#FC6255")
        parabola_label = MathTex("y = x^2", color="#FC6255").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(parabola_label, "B5")

        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(parabola), Write(parabola_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Points and secant line
        p1 = axes.c2p(1, 1)
        p2 = axes.c2p(2, 4)
        dot1 = Dot(p1, color=WHITE)
        dot2 = Dot(p2, color=WHITE)
        secant = Line(axes.c2p(0.5, 0.25), axes.c2p(2.2, 4.6), color=WHITE)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(dot1), FadeIn(dot2), Create(secant))
        self.wait(1)

        # Magnifying glass circle
        mag_circle = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#E6E6E6", stroke_width=4).move_to(p1)
        self.play(Create(mag_circle))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Zooming in (Step 1)
        zoomed_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0.8, 1.2, 0.1],
            y_range=[0.6, 1.4, 0.2],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY_D},
            x_length=5,
            y_length=5
        )
        self.place_in_area(zoomed_axes, "A1", "F6")
        zoomed_parabola = zoomed_axes.plot(lambda x: x**2, x_range=[0.8, 1.2], color="#FC6255")
        
        # Expand circle to act as a frame
        mag_circle_target = Circle(radius=2.8, color="#E6E6E6", stroke_width=2).move_to(zoomed_axes.get_center())

        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(axes, zoomed_axes),
            ReplacementTransform(parabola, zoomed_parabola),
            ReplacementTransform(mag_circle, mag_circle_target),
            FadeOut(secant),
            FadeOut(dot2),
            FadeOut(parabola_label),
            dot1.animate.move_to(zoomed_axes.c2p(1, 1)),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Even more zoom (Step 2)
        final_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0.95, 1.05, 0.025],
            y_range=[0.9, 1.1, 0.05],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY_D},
            x_length=5,
            y_length=5
        )
        self.place_in_area(final_axes, "A1", "F6")
        final_parabola = final_axes.plot(lambda x: x**2, x_range=[0.95, 1.05], color="#FC6255")

        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(zoomed_axes, final_axes),
            ReplacementTransform(zoomed_parabola, final_parabola),
            dot1.animate.move_to(final_axes.c2p(1, 1)),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Tangent line and Slope
        tangent = final_axes.plot(lambda x: 2*x - 1, x_range=[0.95, 1.05], color="#FFFF00")
        # Removing \text{} to prevent LaTeX compilation errors in restricted environments
        slope_label = MathTex("slope", "=", "2", color="#FFFF00").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(slope_label, "D5")

        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(Create(tangent), Write(slope_label))
        self.wait(2)
